summary: Created back/tools/audit_llm_deviation.py — a standalone multi-day LLM appraisal deviation audit script. The script runs a controlled N-day simulation (default 5, minimum 5), builds AppraisalInput objects for T1/T2/T4 from the pre-day snapshot state following the same structural patterns as tick_bridge.py, calls comparison_harness.run_comparison() for each tick, and records the full ComparisonReport including raw LLM response, parsed/shadow output, deterministic baseline output, and the ComparisonVerdict. Results are aggregated into a structured JSON file (p33_t1_deviation_audit.json) and a human-readable markdown report (p33_t1_deviation_report.md). The script handles LLM failures gracefully (records as LLM_CONNECTION_FAILURE or LLM_PARSE_FAILURE data points, never aborts), fails clearly with an explanatory message if ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is missing, and does not modify any engine/domain/service files. All 928 existing tests pass.
commands_run: python3 -c "import ast; ast.parse(open('tools/audit_llm_deviation.py').read()); print('syntax OK')"  # syntax check
python3 -m pytest tests/ --tb=short -q  # full test suite — 928 passed
python3 -c "... all imports in the script ..."  # import resolution check
python3 tools/audit_llm_deviation.py --days 5  # dry-run — fails clearly with missing API key message
unresolved_issues: The audit script cannot be actually run in this session because ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is not set in the execution environment. The script's correctness was verified via: (1) syntax check, (2) import resolution, (3) dry-run producing the expected error message, and (4) full test suite passing. The script will produce audit_outputs/p33_t1_deviation_audit.json and audit_outputs/p33_t1_deviation_report.md when run with a valid key.

Minor state-slicing simplification: AppraisalInputs for T1, T2, T4 are built from pre-day snapshot state rather than the mid-day state tick_bridge uses internally (T2 uses state after T1 ran, T4 uses state after T1+T2+T3 ran). This is an accepted and documented simplification — the audit discloses it prominently in the report header. It does not affect relative deviation analysis since both the LLM call and the deterministic baseline use the same input.
